01/05/2025
The claimant reported a low-speed head-on collision and stated that the policyholder's vehicle was struck while
stopped in a lane. The claimant is now represented by an attorney, so all further contact will go through counsel.
01/17/2025
Police confirmed the claimant was seated in the vehicle at the scene, and two independent witnesses have given
statements consistent with the reported sequence of events. The other driver also described the collision the same
way.
01/30/2025
Scene photographs and the damage to the vehicle line up with the described impact. Nothing in the file suggests the
damage predates the policy's effective date.
02/17/2025
The driver is listed as a named insured on the policy, and the coverage was in force at the time of loss. No prior
damage to the vehicle appears in our records or in the inspection report.
04/08/2025
The claimant reported neck and back strain shortly after the collision, which fits the type and force of impact seen in
the photographs. Medical records from the first visit describe pain consistent with that injury.
04/09/2025
Initial treatment was modest, but over the following weeks the frequency of visits increased to nearly daily, and the
volume of care is now well beyond what is usual for a strain of this kind. Pain was later reported in additional areas of
the body that were not mentioned at the first visit.
05/03/2025
Our search of prior claims and medical history found no earlier injury to the same areas of the neck and back. The
claimant's prior records show no comparable complaints.
05/08/2025
In a recorded follow-up, the claimant added some minor details about the position of the vehicles and the sequence of
braking, but the core account has remained the same across every statement given so far.
06/04/2025
Counsel has requested an evaluation of the claim and has asked that the carrier direct questions through the firm. I
have acknowledged the request and noted the file accordingly.
06/09/2025
I reviewed the treatment plan with the file and noted that the number of providers and the scope of therapy have
expanded since the claim was opened. I have asked for the treating physician's rationale for the additional areas.
07/31/2025
The claim file has been reviewed against the photographs, witness statements, police report, and vehicle inspection.
The accounts agree with one another, and the physical evidence supports the reported impact.

List the facts written on this page. Copy each value exactly as it is written: same spelling,
punctuation and date format. Do not add anything that is not on this page. Use "" for a missing value.

Person "role" must be one of: claimant, attorney, defense_attorney, expert, doctor, officer, adjuster, witness, other.
  claimant = the person who made the claim (also called patient, plaintiff, client, customer,
  or the driver who reported it). attorney = a lawyer for the claimant or plaintiff.
  defense_attorney = a lawyer for the insurance company or defendant.
Organization "type" must be one of: repair_shop, clinic, law_firm, court, insurer, police, other.
"policy_numbers" = only values labeled as a policy number. A claim number is not a policy number.
"street" and "city" = the person's own home address, only if the page gives it. Never use the
address of a clinic, shop, firm or court for a person.
"loss_dates" = only a date that the page clearly gives as the date of the accident, crash, loss or
injury. Do not list the date of a note, letter, report, visit, statement, filing or signature.
"words_before" = the words written on the page directly before that date, copied exactly, that say
it is the loss date. Examples: "Date of loss:", "Crash date:", "Date of injury:", "the collision on".
